numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For x = 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10), the comparison x > 20 evaluates to False, and the precision loss makes log(1 + 1e-10) round to 0 when 1 is added to the tiny difference at working precision; diff = x - 20 evaluated at low precision (2 digits) gives 1.0E-10 instead of the accurate value.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: x > 20 should evaluate to True, since x = 20 + log(1 + 10**-10) is greater than 20; N(x) should give 20.0000000001000 and the difference x - 20 should be about 9.99999999950000E-11 at default precision.
trigger_conditions: argument of log is extremely close to 1 (e.g. 1 + S(10)**-10)
lhs and rhs of the numeric inequality are sufficiently close so that high precision is needed
evaluation at low working precision such as diff.evalf(2)
in the pre-fix code the branch computing arg - 1 separately was not taken when re == fzero or no accuracy check was made
oracle_clues: diff.evalf() with default precision should give 9.99999999950000E-11
the PR states a regression test was added
issue #28514 concerns precision error in evalf of log(y/z) where strict=True should raise a precision error instead of returning 0

numerical_characteristics.precision: Default precision evaluates 1 + 10**-10 to exactly 1, losing the small term; PR diff with default precision gives 9.99999999950000E-11 and with low precision (2 digits) gives 1.0E-10; issue #28514 uses strict=True with maxn=1e300 and reports log(y/z) evaluating to 0 versus expected -1.00000000000000e-22 from log(y)-log(z)
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Arguments near 1 such as 1 + 10**-10 and 1 + 10**-9 (differences of about 1e-10 and 1e-9); issue #28514 uses b = 1e-22
category_specific_evidence: Property violated: log(1 + eps) must be nonzero and positive for small eps>0, so 20 + log(1 + 10**-10) must be greater than 20; the buggy code returned log(1) = 0 and x > 20 evaluated to False

Issue #28514: log(y/z) with y = b/(b+1), z = b should equal log(y) - log(z) = log(1/(b+1)) ≈ -b; the single-expression evaluation printed 0 while the split form printed -1.00000000000000e-22, and the issue states it should raise a precision error under strict=True
Regression test test_issue_28280 asserts 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-10) > 20 and 20 + log(1 + S(10)**-9) > 20
Fix in evalf_log: computes x-1 accurately via evalf_add, checks xre_acc, then adds 1 back at increased working precision prec2 = workprec - fastlog(xre)
Issue #28514 closing conclusion: the two expressions behave identically at very high precision within expected numerical error
reproduction_risks: The PR's example output of 9.99999999950000E-11 is printed output from the PR author, not a verified expected value
Issue #28514 reports the wrong result but the passage gives no expected numeric tolerance for the strict-mode check
The discussion raises an open question about xre_acc being None; the passages do not settle whether None means sufficiently accurate
Test name in the diff is test_issue_28280 while the issue discussed is #28514; the passages do not reconcile these identifiers
